companies.name: Larchmere Residential REIT
companies.description: Owns about 14,000 mid-rise apartment units across the Greater Toronto Area and Ottawa. Makes money from monthly rent and parking, and grows by raising rents when tenants turn over.

companies.name: Northgate Living REIT
companies.description: A turnaround story: owns about 9,000 older apartment units in Montréal and Québec City and is renovating them to charge higher rents. Carries more debt than peers while it fixes the portfolio.

companies.name: Bayfront Apartments REIT
companies.description: Owns about 11,000 apartment units in Vancouver suburbs and Calgary. Grew fast by buying buildings with debt, and is now dealing with new supply pulling tenants away.

companies.name: Maple Crest Communities REIT
companies.description: A conservative owner of about 6,500 apartment units in mid-size Ontario cities like Kitchener, London and Hamilton. Known for low debt and slow, steady growth.

companies.name: Riverside Rental Trust
companies.description: A small, fast-growing trust that buys neglected apartment buildings in Atlantic Canada, renovates them and re-leases at higher rents. Growth comes mostly from acquisitions funded with new units and debt.
